description:
Redwood Inference is running a cross-functional “Escalation playbook + known-issues sprint” to reduce customer-impacting time-to-resolution and make support handling more consistent as usage scales across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The project refreshes (1) escalation paths and ownership boundaries between Support/CS, SRE/Oncall, Runtime, Private Deployments, and Security; (2) support SLAs and severity definitions by customer tier; and (3) a curated, searchable set of top known issues with validated workarounds published into the internal knowledge base (and mirrored into public/help content where appropriate).

Goals:
- Standardize severity matrix (P0–P4 / Sev0–Sev3), routing rules, and “what constitutes an escalation” for common failure modes (5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnects, throttling/429s, Dedicated capacity shortfalls, Private networking/SSO/audit-log issues).
- Align Support response SLAs, engineering engagement SLAs, and customer comms expectations by tier (self-serve vs dedicated vs private/enterprise), including first response, investigation updates, and mitigation timelines.
- Publish a “Known Issues & Workarounds” set that Support can confidently use during triage, including customer-facing safe mitigations (SDK retry guidance, timeouts, streaming reconnects, model pinning/rollbacks, region failover hints) and internal-only diagnostics.
- Drive a short execution sprint to close/mitigate the highest-volume escalations (via runbook improvements, alert tuning, incident-bot automation, and docs/SDK fixes).

Scope and phases (4 weeks, Feb–Mar 2026):
1) Discovery + data pull (week 1): top ticket themes, repeat escalations, gaps in runbooks and comms, SLA mismatches.
2) Draft playbook + SLA tables + templates (week 2): Support/CS and SRE sign-off.
3) Known-issues sprint execution (week 2–3): targeted fixes (docs + small product/ops improvements), validate workarounds, publish KB pages.
4) Rollout + training (week 4): announce changes, run Support training, update Jira templates/macros, define ownership for ongoing upkeep.

Primary stakeholders and roles:
- Exec sponsor: Jasmine Liu (VP Customer Success)
- Program lead: Dev Patel (Director, Customer Support)
- Docs lead: Elliot Price (Director, Technical Documentation) with Kira Thompson / Wei Chen
- Reliability lead: Sean Gallagher (Director of SRE) with Rafael Mendes
- Key contributors: Owen Phillips, Priya Shah (Support Engineering); Miles Thornton / Tomáš Novák (SRE); Alex Martinez (VP DevEx) for doc-site/SDK guidance
- Partner teams: Product Ops (Chris Osei) for reporting cadence; Engineering owners as-needed (runtime/platform/private deployments)

Deliverables:
- Confluence escalation playbook (severity, SLAs, who-to-page, handoff criteria, templates, examples).
- Updated support process docs and Jira ticket templates/fields guidance.
- Known issues catalog with validated workarounds (internal + “safe to share” excerpts).
- Linear sprint plan and task breakdown; linked GitHub PRs and Jira tickets.
- Training artifacts (slides/agenda), and comms in Slack/Announcements.

Constraints:
- Customer-identifying details must be handled as restricted where needed (especially for Private/enterprise incidents).
- Workarounds must be validated (no speculative mitigations) and tagged by applicability (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, region/model/runtime version).
- Escalation policy must be compatible with existing SRE oncall/incident process and paging hygiene goals.

files.description: Playbook landing page: purpose, guiding principles, definitions, links to severity/SLAs, and the end-to-end escalation flow from Support intake to Eng/SRE engagement and resolution.
Severity matrix (P0–P4 / Sev0–Sev3) with concrete examples for inference failures (5xx, timeouts, streaming drops, data issues, security/SSO outages) and triage checklist.
SLA tables by customer tier (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise): first response, update frequency, time-to-mitigation targets, after-hours coverage expectations, and escalation triggers.
Ownership map: which team owns which component (api-gateway, scheduler, serving-runtime, auth/rbac, private installer) and how Support routes issues; includes paging rules and backup contacts.
Copy/paste templates for customer updates: investigation started, mitigation applied, monitoring, RCA commitment, and closure; includes tone guidance and what not to promise.
Support ticket standards: required fields (impact, env/region, model, request ids, logs), reproduction steps, and how to link Slack/incident/GitHub artifacts for efficient escalation.
How Support hands off to SRE/oncall: when to declare an incident, what information is required, how to use #incidents, and how to keep the customer loop updated.
Known issues catalog index: tagging scheme (product, model family, region, runtime version), ‘safe-to-share’ flag, and links to individual issue pages and workaround decision trees.
Known issue page: streaming disconnect symptoms, common causes, recommended client retry/reconnect patterns, timeouts, and log fields to request from customers.
Known issue page: 429s, quota/rate-limit confusion, how to verify org/project limits, and standard mitigations (burst settings, backoff, Dedicated options).
Known issue page: Dedicated latency spikes during peak load; diagnostic steps, dashboards to check, and mitigation options (autoscaling knobs, isolation, routing/fallback policies).
Alignment doc between Support and incident comms: when to post status updates, what can be shared, and how Support mirrors incident updates in customer threads.
Working doc: kickoff notes, unresolved policy questions (SLAs, after-hours), list of stakeholders to review, and initial draft outline for Confluence pages.
Spreadsheet-style table: top ticket drivers by volume/impact (timeouts, streaming, 429s, Private SSO), links to representative Jira tickets, and proposed fixes/workarounds.
Backlog tracker for known-issues pages: owner, validation status, customer-facing wording review, and publish dates; ties to Linear tasks and GitHub PRs.
Training deck: new severity rules, SLA expectations, escalation flow, and scenario-based exercises for triage/escalation (with answer key and links to KB pages).
Joint Support+SRE metrics sheet: MTTA/MTTR for escalations, paging volume, gaps between customer SLAs and internal SLOs; proposes alert and runbook improvements.
Linear project ticket: ‘Known-issues sprint’ umbrella with goals, success metrics (ticket deflection, MTTR), scope, and sub-issues for docs, tooling, and SRE improvements.
Task: Add ‘escalation required fields’ lint/checklist to Support workflow (links to Confluence), including request-id capture and environment/model metadata.
Task: Incident-bot automation for support escalations (auto-create #incidents thread stub, collect required fields, and post comms reminder templates).
Task: Improve observability for streaming disconnects (add new metric + dashboard panel + runbook link surfaced to Support).
Task: Dedicated capacity ‘latency spike’ diagnostic runbook refresh and alert tuning to reduce false pages.
PM ticket: Confirm external-facing SLA language and customer commitments by tier; coordinate with CRO/CS leadership and validate any legal constraints.
PM ticket: Approve ‘safe-to-share’ wording for top known-issues pages and define criteria for when issues should be published vs kept internal.
Customer ticket (enterprise/dedicated): intermittent streaming disconnects in us-east; includes logs, request ids, timeline, escalation to SRE, and workaround validation.
Customer ticket (self-serve): frequent 429s after launch; confusion about rate limits and retries; resolved with quota review and client backoff guidance.
Customer ticket (private): SSO/SAML login failures after IdP change; requires Security/Private Deployments escalation; includes comms cadence and mitigation steps.
Customer ticket (dedicated): latency spikes during peak hours; suspected noisy-neighbor/capacity; links to dashboards and proposed tuning; follow-up for Dedicated sizing.
Customer ticket (enterprise/hosted): increased 5xx in eu-west for a pinned model version; results in region failover guidance and an internal incident reference.
Internal ticket: update Jira support project fields/templates to match new escalation required fields, SLA due dates, and link conventions.
Internal ticket: create Support macro/snippet library for common comms templates (investigation, mitigation, closure) and ensure restricted handling for sensitive accounts.
PR: Add ‘Support Escalation’ workflow to incident-bot (form prompts, required field enforcement, links to Confluence playbook, optional Jira key capture).
PR: Add escalation-related SLO views (time-to-ack, time-to-mitigation) and export for weekly Support+SRE review.
PR: New dashboard panels/alerts for streaming disconnect rate and timeout rate, with runbook links and region/model breakdowns.
PR: Publish/refresh KB pages for streaming reconnect guidance, 429 troubleshooting, and Dedicated latency spike diagnostics; includes review from Support and Docs.
PR: Improve default retry/backoff guidance and surface better error messages for 429/timeouts; references known-issues pages and support tickets.
PR: Small runtime/edge fix related to streaming stability (e.g., better handling of client disconnects / keepalive) tied to escalations; includes rollout notes.
Thread: Support triage discussion on new required fields for escalations; questions about request-id capture, what to ask customers, and linking Jira/Slack.
Thread: Live escalation for 429 spike; Support/CS coordinate comms, confirm quota settings, and decide whether to engage SRE.
Thread: Enterprise CSM asks for SLA clarification and after-hours expectations for a Dedicated customer; Dev Patel and SRE weigh in.
Thread: Oncall feedback on proposed escalation policy; concern about paging hygiene and what should be incident vs support escalation.
Thread: SRE reviews draft SLA tables; aligns internal SLO targets, update frequency, and incident declaration criteria.
Thread: Docs review of known-issues wording (‘safe to share’); discussion of what belongs in public docs vs internal Confluence.
Thread: Incident-adjacent escalation where Support requests a formal incident for elevated 5xx; includes incident-bot prompts and comms cadence coordination.
Thread: Announcement of Escalation Playbook v2 rollout, new SLAs, training session times, and links to Confluence/Drive materials.
Email thread: Dev Patel coordinating reviews and approvals for Escalation Playbook v2 with Jasmine Liu, Sean Gallagher, and Elliot Price; includes links to drafts and deadlines.
Email thread: CS leadership alignment on enterprise SLA language and exception handling; loop-in to CRO (Jordan Blake) for customer expectation management.
Email thread: Docs team publishing plan for known issues; review checklist, ‘restricted vs internal’ classification, and coordination with Support Engineers.
Email thread: SRE leadership feedback on escalation thresholds to prevent alert fatigue; proposes runbook improvements and a pilot period.
Transcript: Support/CS/SRE working session to finalize severity matrix, escalation triggers, and comms update cadence; ends with action items and owners.
Transcript: Retro with CS and Support after a recent enterprise escalation; identifies gaps in request metadata, dashboards, and workaround documentation.
Company record: Enterprise customer with Dedicated deployment; notes recurring latency spike escalations, linked SUP tickets, stakeholders (AE/CSM), and next steps.
Company record: Private/VPC customer; notes SSO/audit-log requirements, recent support escalation, security review status, and linked artifacts (Fireflies/Gmail/Jira).
Company record: High-growth self-serve account hitting 429s/timeouts; notes recommended retry guidance, quota changes, and upgrade path to Dedicated.
